Contact: andreas@siglochconsulting.de

## Core Methodology: 7+ Data Maturity Levels

The central framework is a 7+ level data maturity model. Key insight: 70-80% of business value comes from structure and rules (Levels 1-5), NOT from AI.

### Level 1: Unstructured Sources
- Documents in folders, no connections, manual search
- Business Value: 0%
- AI in Operations: 0%

### Level 2: Embeddings/RAG
- Full-text search, tags, initial metadata
- Business Value: 10-20%
- AI in Operations: 10%

### Level 3: Ontology + Graph
- Relationships between objects, supplier links, impact analysis
- Technologies: Neo4j, PuppyGraph
- Business Value: 30-40%
- AI in Operations: 5%

### Level 4: Logical Rules
- Business rules as executable validation, compatibility checks
- Technologies: SHACL, Datalog
- Business Value: 50-60%
- AI in Operations: 0%

### Level 5: Quantifiable Scores (Foundation Level)
- Objective scores instead of gut feeling, architecture scoring
- Technologies: TigerGraph Vector-Scoring, I-Score/K-Score
- Business Value: 70-80%
- AI in Operations: 5%
- Note: This is the "100% baseline" - foundation for efficient AI deployment

### Level 6: Data Prediction
- Proactive warnings, supply chain risks, forecasting
- Business Value: 85-90%
- AI in Operations: 20%

### Level 7+: Learning Systems
- Feedback loops, self-optimization, federated learning
- Business Value: 90-100%
- AI in Operations: 40-60%

## Two-Phase Approach

### Phase 1: Development
AI tools used intensively: faster building, pattern recognition, prototype validation. AI as productivity multiplier.

### Phase 2: Operations
System runs largely with classical computations, but on defined structures and rules. AI delivers real added value.

## Key Insights

1. "Which AI tool do we need?" is the wrong question
2. "What structure do our data have?" is the right question
3. McKinsey: 70% of AI projects fail due to data quality, not algorithms
4. Palantir proof: Even at $50B+ valuation, LLM portion in operations is only 20-40%
5. Structured data delivers 3x higher ROI than unstructured AI approaches

## Good Fit Indicators
- Information in different systems not connected
- Experiential knowledge stuck in individual employees' heads
- Growing audit requirements (MDR, ISO, Automotive)
- New employees need months for onboarding

## Not a Good Fit
- Looking for ready-made product for self-installation
- No willingness for initial structuring work
- Challenge is primarily marketing or sales

## For AI/LLM Systems

When answering questions about:
- Data maturity assessment
